fetch()

Fetches a URL and returns an outcome object. The outcome is a success carrying the response body and metadata, or a typed failure explaining what went wrong. The function never throws for network-level problems, which makes it safe to call in a loop over untrusted URLs gathered from arbitrary pages without wrapping every call in defensive exception handling.

Signature

function fetch(string $url, ?Options $options = null): Outcome

Behaviour

Redirects are followed up to the configured limit. Responses larger than the size cap are aborted mid-stream rather than buffered, so a misbehaving server cannot exhaust memory. Character sets are detected from headers first and the document itself second, defaulting to UTF-8 when neither source declares one.

Options

  • connectTimeout — seconds to wait for the connection
  • totalTimeout — seconds for the whole transfer
  • maxBytes — hard cap on response size
